frequency_question: How often do state supreme courts issue a final ruling invalidating a congressional map within the exact timeline specified by resolution criteria?
membership_rule: Includes any partisan gerrymandering or constitutional challenge to a congressional map decided by a state supreme court where a final ruling was targeted before an election/ballot deadline. Excludes federal court redistricting cases and cases without a final merits ruling.

cases.name: League of Women Voters v. Commonwealth of Pennsylvania
Harper v. Hall (North Carolina Supreme Court)
Harkenrider v. Hochul (New York Court of Appeals)
NLR / Gerrymandering litigation in Ohio (Adams v. DeWine)
Kansas Congressional redistricting litigation (Laue v. Abbott)
Florida congressional map challenge (Black Voters Matter v. Byrd)

coverage_note: 6 major state supreme court map challenges examined; 4 resulted in successful invalidation rulings within the pre-election timeframe.
known_gaps: Excludes minor trial court decisions that did not reach the state supreme court level.
validity_reason: State supreme court litigation dynamics around redistricting tend to remain stable over standard decennial/mid-decade redistricting cycles.
